title: A quarter to nine
subtopic: S10 — The bag, the cab, the rain and the train
learning_goal: Know what a Bradshaw was, what a hansom was, what the fog really was and what a guinea really was — and that London still has working gas lamps.

narration.script: Almost no luggage — a fifth of his fortune in cash. That red book is a Bradshaw: the world's first compiled railway timetable, 1839, sixpence. By 1872, hundreds of pages of trains and steamers: the internet of the age, in a satchel. A hansom: two wheels, the driver perched behind and above you, a hatch in the roof. Sixpence a mile. He gives her the twenty guineas he won at cards, without breaking stride. Four hundred and twenty shillings: eight hundred miles of cab at sixpence a mile. A sum, not a coin: a price that outlived its own money, and still how Savile Row quotes a suit. Tonight it simply rains. The famous pea-soupers were winter coal-smoke, not weather; the worst killed prize cattle at Smithfield the next year. About thirteen hundred gas lamps still burn in London, tended by lamplighters. Past New Cross the valet remembers the gas burning in his room. It will burn for eighty days, at his master's expense.

production_notes: SLOT CONVENTION (film rev 2): every media entry's start_s/end_s are SCENE-CLOCK seconds — where the shot sits in this scene — not in/out points in the source file. A source in-point, where one is needed, is written in that entry's note as 'source in-point mm:ss'. Slots are contiguous and cover 0 s to duration_s with no gaps and no overlaps; audio beds are the only entries allowed to span other slots. Four of the twenty visual slots carry a mandatory date in the caption line (M-29, M-28, M-81, M-27) — that is the picture's own furniture, never a floating overlay.

Scene Developer + Narrator, film rev 2, 2026-09-08. Block S10 (118 s, 20 visual slots, word cap 170).
SENTENCE ↔ SLOT: 'Almost no luggage…' over slots 1–2 · 'That red book is a Bradshaw…' over slot 3, ending by 17 s so the timetable page holds 5 s · 'A hansom: two wheels…' over slots 5–6 · SILENCE 34–46 (slot 7, Donisthorpe 1890, all twelve seconds) · 'He gives her the twenty guineas…' over slot 8, ending by 55 s so the plate holds 5 s · 'A sum, not a coin…' over slots 10–11 · 'Tonight it simply rains…' over slots 12–13 · 'About thirteen hundred gas lamps…' over slots 14–15 · SILENCE 94–106 (slots 16–17, the platform and the whistle) · 'Past New Cross the valet remembers…' over slots 18–19.
COORDINATOR'S OVERLAY MIGRATION — TAKEN: 'Twenty guineas — 420 shillings, or 840 cab-miles' was an overlay and overlays are gone; the arithmetic is now spoken ('Four hundred and twenty shillings — eight hundred miles of cab at sixpence a mile'). The rundown's own figure is eight hundred, derived as 420 shillings ÷ 6d = 840 and rounded down; I have used the rundown's rounded number and flagged the discrepancy for the Fact-Checker (F-12 + F-28).
TRUTH ON SCREEN (L7): M-81 'Trafalgar Square, 1890' and M-27 '1905' are mandatory; I have also dated M-28 (1877) and M-29 (c. 1891–96), which the rundown did not require but which cost nothing and are the same principle.
PROVISIONAL: G-07 exists but must stop being a game · C-24 is a pending card · S-brad and S-gas have no source · N3d and N3e have no source and nothing was invented for them — the film's last minute currently rests on two pending-asset slots with M-27 and M-88 as fallbacks.
